chunks: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Sandal, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The fulfilment of a need of a believer is more beloved to Allah than performing twenty Hajj, each time its performer spending one hundred thousand (dirhams).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a believer in their needs compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the act of fulfilling a believer's need above the monumental virtue of twenty Hajj pilgrimages, each marked by substantial financial sacrifice of one hundred thousand dirhams. This comparison underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on social solidarity and practical assistance (kafā'at al-ḥājah) as a direct, high-yield path to divine pleasure, often viewed as more immediate and accessible than the ritualistic excellence of pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, from Sandal, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The fulfilment of a need of an affair of a Momin is more Beloved to Allahazwj than performing twenty Hajj, its performer having spent during each Hajj, one hundred thousand (Dirhams)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Sandal from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani

from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘To help meet the needs of a believing man is more beloved to Allah than twenty Hajj for which one spends one hundred thousand.’”
